status_when_frozen: No window listed here had been run or analysed. All hypotheses, thresholds and decision rules below were fixed from the exploratory replay of the 15 runs of 12 October 2026 (single 48-h window, live orbital elements), which is reported separately as exploratory.
unit_of_analysis: analysis window (one 48-h window per run); onsets and cloud realisations are nested within it

settings.h1_floor_margin: one orbital period at the fleet's median altitude

hypotheses.H1a: Latency non-inferiority of the earliest-completion cover (ECC, k = 30): in a window, the share of evaluable onsets at which ECC reaches 95% of the tiles reachable in the onset's 24-h horizon no later than one orbital period after the physical floor (clear sky). Claim: the mean of this share over windows is at least 90%.
hypotheses.H1b: Image economy of ECC: in a window, the share of eligible onsets (first-come-first-served needs two or more images to reach the level) at which ECC meets the H1a criterion with fewer images than first-come-first-served. Claim: the mean of this share over windows is at least 90%.
hypotheses.H2: Value of acting on cloud observations: in a window, the mean over 20 cloud realisations (correlated model, L = 50 km, T = 3 h, p = 0.35) of the coverage difference, adaptive selector minus the same planner run in advance without observations, both with the same number of images (time-aware objective). Claim: the mean of this difference over windows is above 0.

evaluability.rule_onsets: a window counts for H1a/H1b only with at least 29 evaluated (resp. eligible) onsets
evaluability.rule_h2: a window counts for H2 only when H2 is evaluable in it (the selector adapted at least once and the greedy given the cloud beats the open-loop plan in some realisation)

decision_rules.H1a_H1b: SUPPORTED if the one-sided (1 - alpha') Student-t lower confidence bound of the mean over evaluable windows is >= 90%; NOT SUPPORTED otherwise; NOT EVALUABLE with fewer than 5 evaluable windows
decision_rules.H2: SUPPORTED if the one-sided (1 - alpha') Student-t lower confidence bound of the mean over evaluable windows is > 0 coverage points; NOT SUPPORTED otherwise; NOT EVALUABLE with fewer than 5 evaluable windows
decision_rules.alpha_prime: alpha / 3 (Bonferroni over the three primary hypotheses) for the primary design; alpha for secondary designs, which are exploratory

deviations_policy: Any change to code, settings, windows or rules after freezing is reported as a deviation with its reason; results under the frozen plan are reported regardless.

amendments.reason: Points a referee is expected to raise. (1) H1a is met at every onset with the protocol's budget of 30 images because earliest-completion cover (ECC) searches from the physical floor, so H1a shows that the budget suffices; smaller budgets show where it starts to bind. (2) The archive validation (Cell 7D) recorded near-zero scene cloud cover in these dry-season windows, against the protocol's constant cloud probability of 0.35; the per-tile climatology option of the release shows H2 under a realistic probability. (3) H1b failed in one window (14 September) through ties with first-come-first-served; the exact minimum number of images at each onset shows whether any selector could have used fewer. (4) The exact optimum was measured on 6-h sub-problems only; one full-window instance per window measures ECC's greedy cover against the exact minimum at full scale and repeats the confirmatory run otherwise (determinism check).

amendments.question: What sets the physical floor: the wait for the first usable pass, the coverage geometry, or delivery?
amendments.method: Each onset's floor (95% of reachable cells, clear sky, 24-h horizon) split exactly into W (onset to the first acquisition with a usable cell), G (that acquisition to the acquisition of the pass that completes the level) and L (acquisition to delivery of that pass); sun elevation at the region's centroid at the onset from the pipeline's NOAA routine. Every floor and reachable count is recomputed from arf_refined_events.csv and must equal arf_onset_robustness.csv, or the script stops.

amendments.status_when_amended: POST HOC. Written after the confirmatory results and A4 to A11 were read, to bound the first limitation (every daylight PlanetScope pass assumed to acquire). While the script was tested, it was run on the window of 3 August 2026 (sandbox copy of that run, 20 seeds): H1a share 100% at every fraction; H1b share 100, 96.5, 84.0 and 52.9% at f = 1, 0.75, 0.5 and 0.25; median floor unchanged at 12.1 h. No other window has been replayed.
amendments.question: How do the floor, the reachable share and the H1a and H1b shares change if only a fraction f of PlanetScope's predicted daylight passes acquire an image?
amendments.method: A PlanetScope pass is a maximal run of consecutive minutes of one FLOCK satellite. Per seed (1 to 20) each pass gets one uniform draw u and acquires when u < f (nested fractions f = 1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25); Sentinel-2 and Landsat passes are always kept. Per onset, the floor, reachable count, ECC (k = 30) and FCFS image count are recomputed with the rules of Cell 7C; at f = 1 every onset must equal the run's arf_onset_robustness.csv (floor, reachable, ECC time, ECC images, FCFS images), or the script stops. H1a and H1b shares by the protocol's rules, margin = the run's t_max_wait_min.
amendments.scope: Read-only replay of the 8 primary dry-season windows (3 Aug to 21 Sep 2026) and the 8 wet-season windows of A5 (5 Jan to 23 Feb 2026, p = 0.35 runs). Descriptive sensitivity analysis; no hypothesis, no decision changes. It bounds the acquisition assumption from the model side; it does not measure Planet's acquisition fraction, which needs catalogue metadata.
